title: Double-Shear Safety of a Weight-Stack Selector Pin During a Lat Pulldown
studentDocumentTitle: Student Packet - Weight-Stack Selector Pin in Double Shear
instructorDocumentTitle: Instructor Guide - Weight-Stack Selector Pin in Double Shear
summary: Evaluate a weight-stack selector pin for average double-shear stress, factor of safety against shear yielding, and minimum required diameter.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference section view and free-body diagram of a weight-stack selector pin loaded symmetrically in double shear.
problemStatement:
A fitness-equipment engineering team is checking the horizontal selector pin that connects a cable-driven selector stem to a selected portion of a lat-pulldown weight stack. The selected stack setting is Ws = {{selector_W_lb}} {{selector_W_lb_unit}}. During controlled constant-speed lifting, the pin is idealized as a circular connector in symmetric double shear, with the central selector stem loading the pin and the selected plate supporting it on two sides.

This introductory check assumes two equally loaded shear planes through the smooth pin shank. It neglects pin bending, bearing and tear-out, fatigue, wear, clearance and impact effects, friction, cable/pulley losses, and local stress concentrations.
engineeringGoal: Determine the average double-shear stress and factor of safety against shear yielding for the {{selector_d_mm}} {{selector_d_mm_unit}} pin, then determine the minimum diameter required to satisfy FSreq = {{selector_FS_req}} and make a bounded engineering recommendation.
